'''Alastair Oliver Scott''' (born 18 September 1965) is a New Zealand politician who was elected to the New Zealand parliament at the [[2014 New Zealand general election|2014 general election]] as a representative of the [[New Zealand National Party]].

==Private life and business interests==
Scott grew up in [[Auckland]] and [[Wellington]] attending Wellington College and then [[Massey University]] in [[Palmerston North]].<ref name="Matahiwi profile">{{cite web |title=Our People |url= http://matahiwi.co.nz/our-story/our-people/|publisher=Matahiwi Estate |accessdate=10 October 2014}}</ref> He is the owner of the Matahiwi Estate winery.<ref name="WTA profile" />

Scott and his partner Robyn Noble-Campbell share their time between homes in the [[Wellington]] suburb of [[Kelburn, New Zealand|Kelburn]] (their primary home) and [[Masterton]].<ref name="can't vote">{{cite news |last1=Farmer |first1=Don |title=Scott can't vote for himself |url= http://www.nzherald.co.nz/wairarapa-times-age/news/article.cfm?c_id=1503414&objectid=11305200 |accessdate=28 September 2014 |work=[[Wairarapa Times-Age]] |date=7 August 2014}}</ref> Both of them have three children each.<ref name="WTA profile" /><ref name="can't vote" />

Scott defeated [[Jo Hayes]] to win the National Party's selection for the {{NZ electorate link|Wairarapa}} electorate at the [[2014 New Zealand general election|2014 election]].<ref name="WTA profile">{{cite news| url= http://www.nzherald.co.nz/wairarapa-times-age/news/article.cfm?c_id=1503414&objectid=11244404 |title=Winery boss gains party's nomination |work=[[Wairarapa Times-Age]] |date=26 April 2014 |accessdate=28 September 2014 |first=Elliot |last=Parker}}</ref> The late entry of [[Carterton, New Zealand|Carterton]] mayor and former MP [[Ron Mark]] for [[New Zealand First]] turned the 2014 election into a "three-horse race" with Labour's [[Kieran McAnulty]] and Scott.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Fuller |first1=Piers |title=Wairarapa's three-horse race on final straight |url= http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/10507839/Wairarapas-three-horse-race-on-final-straight |accessdate=10 October 2014 |work=[[Stuff.co.nz]] |agency=Wairarapa News |date=17 September 2014}}</ref> In the end, Scott had a clear majority over McAnulty, with Mark slightly behind in third place.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Taylor |first1=Cherie |title='Huge' win for new Wairarapa MP |url= http://www.nzherald.co.nz/wairarapa-times-age/news/article.cfm?c_id=1503414&objectid=11329141 |accessdate=10 October 2014 |work=[[Wairarapa Times-Age]] |date=22 September 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Official Count Results -- Wairarapa |url=http://electionresults.org.nz/electionresults_2014/electorate-58.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |accessdate=10 October 2014 |date=10 October 2014 |archive-date=16 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141016124436/http://electionresults.org.nz/electionresults_2014/electorate-58.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He won the Wairarapa seat again in the [[2017 New Zealand general election]] with a reduced majority, and placed 46th on the party list.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Boyle |first1=Chelsea |title=Scott holds off challenge |url= https://times-age.co.nz/scott-holds-off-challenge/ |accessdate=19 April 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Official Count Results -- Wairarapa |url= http://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2017/electorate-details-58.html |publisher = [[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |accessdate=19 April 2018}}</ref>

On 25 June 2019, Scott announced that he would not contest the [[2020 New Zealand general election|2020 general election]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12243700 |title=National's Amy Adams retiring from politics at 2020 election |date=25 June 2019 |work=New Zealand Herald |accessdate=25 June 2019}}</ref>
